Together these records justify that U has SI exponents L^1 T^-1 and all other base exponents zero, matching the candidate.

The ledger names nu and defines it as kinematic viscosity (dynamic viscosity divided by density). The KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity explicitly defines kinematic viscosity with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 and notes the same definition (dynamic viscosity divided by mass density). This directly supports the candidate exponents (L=2, T=-1; all other bases zero).

The variable x is declared in the problem as the streamwise distance from the leading edge (coordinate along the plate). The KB record pq_streamwise_distance defines streamwise distance as a distance measured along the mean flow direction with SI dimension L, which is the exact physical meaning of x in the Blasius flat-plate problem. Therefore the candidate exponents (L=1, others zero) are correct.

The ledger defines y as the wall-normal distance from the plate (coordinate normal to the plate). The KB record pq_wall_normal_distance explicitly defines wall-normal distance as a distance measured normal to a wall with SI dimension L. This matches the role of y in the Blasius boundary-layer formulation and supports the candidate exponents (L=1, others zero).
